hunks.sol: As if something that had sat there like a boulder this whole time was going to start moving now. I tried drawing up my internal energy, but it gave me nothing. I sighed and got to my feet.

hunks.sol: This was the guy who used to move only when I shoved a fist in his face. Somehow, he seemed like a different person.

hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin asked worriedly, “Will he be all right?”

hunks.sol: At first, I thought it was the wind. But those were the cries of living beasts. Hyuk Mujin muttered,

hunks.sol: This was a game set in ancient China. It wouldn’t be strange for wolves or tigers to leap out from anywhere. I’d heard wild animals crying more than once over the past few days.

hunks.baseline: This wasn’t like the ones before. Just hearing those howls made my chest tight and my fingertips tingle.
hunks.sol: This wasn’t like the others. Just hearing those howls made my chest tighten and my fingertips tingle.

hunks.baseline: The gut I’d honed over seven years seemed to whisper. Something was beyond that forest, where the sunlight hadn’t reached yet.
hunks.sol: My instincts, honed over seven years, seemed to whisper that something was waiting beyond that forest, where the sunlight had yet to reach.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin snapped out of it and passed on the order. Three reconnaissance squad members with thin-iron-plated shields blocked the snow-covered path.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin quickly recovered and relayed my order. Three reconnaissance squad members carrying shields clad in thin iron blocked the snow-covered path.

hunks.baseline: A narrow trail, high ground on a hill. Advantageous position.
hunks.sol: A narrow trail and the high ground atop a hill. We had the advantage.

hunks.baseline: A second howl. Closer—and more ominous for it. Hyuk Mujin spoke carefully.
hunks.sol: A second howl rang out. Closer—and all the more ominous for it. Hyuk Mujin spoke carefully.

hunks.baseline: “They appear to be nothing more than a wolf pack…”
hunks.sol: “It sounds like nothing more than a pack of wolves…”

hunks.baseline: I shook my head. We’d been running for two full days. If this brief pause was what got us caught, that was fate.
hunks.sol: I shook my head. We’d been fleeing for two full days. If this brief pause was what got us caught, then it was fate.

hunks.baseline: “Hold. We wait a little longer.”
hunks.sol: “Hold. We’ll wait a little longer.”

hunks.baseline: The beasts seemed to take me at my word. For several minutes the howls never stopped, and they kept getting closer. In the snow-covered mountains at dawn, snapping branches and paws racing over snow made a racket.
hunks.sol: The beasts seemed to understand me. For the next fifteen minutes, the howls continued without pause, drawing ever closer. Snapping branches and paws racing over the snow shattered the stillness of the mountain at dawn.

hunks.baseline: “From the sound, there must be dozens… Wolves are pack animals, but this is strange.”
hunks.sol: “From the sound of it, there must be dozens… Wolves may be pack animals, but this is strange.”

hunks.baseline: No sooner had he finished than the pack showed itself. Maybe they hadn’t found prey in winter; most of them were nothing but ribs. But they were still predators. We couldn’t let our guard down.
hunks.sol: No sooner had he finished than the pack emerged. Maybe they hadn’t been able to find prey in winter; most of them were so gaunt that their ribs showed. But they were still predators. We couldn’t let our guard down.

hunks.baseline: And yet, oddly, I felt relieved. The place was crawling with martial artists, but it wasn’t as if the beasts had learned martial arts too.
hunks.sol: And yet, contrary to my thoughts, I felt oddly relieved. The place might be crawling with martial artists, but surely even the beasts hadn’t learned martial arts.

hunks.baseline: *I skip a few raids and my touch is completely gone.*
hunks.sol: *I skip a few raids and my instincts go completely dull.*

hunks.baseline: I clicked my tongue and stepped forward. The dozens of wolves charging at us already looked like chunks of EXP.
hunks.sol: I clicked my tongue and stepped forward. The dozens of wolves charging toward us already looked like chunks of EXP.

hunks.baseline: I crooked a finger at the wolf running point in the distance. Judging by the size, that one was the leader.
hunks.sol: I crooked a finger at the wolf leading the pack in the distance. Judging by its size, that one had to be the leader.

hunks.baseline: Since when did a wolf roar like a lion? Don’t tell me it was some kind of spirit beast? Was I seriously going to lose to an animal?
hunks.sol: Since when did a wolf roar like a lion? Don’t tell me it was some kind of spirit beast. Was I seriously going to lose to an animal?

hunks.baseline: I swallowed and brought my spear up. I couldn’t afford to lose the battle of wills, so I glared hard and lowered my voice.
hunks.sol: I swallowed and raised my spear. I couldn’t afford to lose the battle of wills, so I glared hard and lowered my voice.

hunks.baseline: The charging wolf suddenly veered off and plunged into the forest. Its dozens of subordinate wolves poured after it.
hunks.sol: The charging wolf suddenly veered aside and plunged into the forest. Its dozens of subordinate wolves poured after it.

hunks.baseline: No—that was a retreat. A cold wind swept over the countless pawprints stamped into the snow.
hunks.sol: No—they had fled. A cold wind swept across the countless pawprints stamped into the snow.

hunks.baseline: *What the hell.*
hunks.sol: *What the hell?*

hunks.baseline: They came running like they were going to eat me alive. Why run?
hunks.sol: They came running like they were going to eat me alive. Why run away?

hunks.baseline: Then a famous comic popped into my head. The one about a rubber man with hyperactivity disorder smashing the maritime authorities.
hunks.sol: Then a certain famous comic popped into my head. The one about a rubber man with hyperactivity disorder smashing the maritime authorities.

hunks.baseline: That ability that could scare enemies senseless—knock them out, even—with qi alone.
hunks.sol: That ability that could terrify enemies—and even knock them unconscious—with qi alone.

hunks.baseline: This game was insane enough that it was entirely possible. In which case the System ought to ping me right about now…
hunks.sol: This game was insane enough for it to be entirely possible. In which case, the System ought to ping me right about now…

hunks.baseline: There it was! I waited for the System voice, buzzing with anticipation.
hunks.sol: There it was! Buzzing with anticipation, I waited for the System voice.

hunks.sol: Ignoring the reconnaissance squad members’ bizarre expressions, I muttered over and over.

hunks.sol: What was happening? Where was I, and who was I?

hunks.sol: Countless questions flashed through my mind and vanished. Then I heard someone’s voice.

hunks.sol: A man stood beside a gaunt tree, more than twenty zhang away.[^1] Far if you called it far, close if you called it close. The problem was that none of us had known he was there.
